criteria.criterion: The doc comment on `pub invocations` in JobRecords (crates/athena-core/src/store.rs) states that steward, audience and auditor runs are not in it and names Records::all_invocations; checked with Grep.
criteria.evidence: I grepped store.rs for 'PARTIAL source|Records::all_invocations' and read lines 29-33. The doc comment on `pub invocations` calls the list a PARTIAL source for measuring usage. It says the steward's, audience's and auditor's runs are never in it and are kept in Records::steward_runs, audience_runs and auditor_runs, and it says a usage measure must read [`Records::all_invocations`]. This text was already in the base.

criteria.criterion: docs/system-facts.md states where each role's runs are recorded (job invocations vs steward_runs, audience_runs, auditor_runs) and that usage measures must read Records::all_invocations; checked with Grep for those names.
criteria.evidence: I grepped docs/system-facts.md, and all five names appear in one fact at lines 45-48. Job runs are in `JobRecords::invocations`. Steward, audience and auditor runs are in `Records::steward_runs`, `audience_runs` and `auditor_runs` and in no job's list. 'A usage measure reads `Records::all_invocations`, and is replayed over records holding those three roles.' This text was already in the base.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core role_need`: a fixture with steward, audience and auditor runs outside job records yields no retire candidate for them (auditor listed as on-demand/not measured), while a genuinely unused in-job role is a candidate, so the measure gives both outcomes. The test fails if role_need reads job.invocations instead of all_invocations.
criteria.evidence: All 11 tests passed. Among them were the new every_role_loaded_through_from_parts_is_counted_and_classified and every_role_is_measured_or_on_demand, and the base tests known_active_roles_are_never_retire_candidates_and_an_unused_role_is and the_measure_yields_both_outcomes_on_a_mixed_fixture, which give the candidate outcome. The new test loads one run of every ALL_ROLES role per job through Records::from_parts, which moves the steward, audience and auditor runs out of the jobs (the test asserts this). It then checks that each role has count > 0, and that each of the three has source SOURCE_OUTSIDE_JOBS, is unflagged, is in not_measured with n > 0, and is not a retire candidate. If compute (role_need.rs:93-136) read job.invocations instead, those three would have no runs, so `count > 0` and the not_measured `n > 0` assertions would fail. I checked this by reading the code. I did not run a mutation, because the role is change-nothing.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core store`: a Records::from_parts test fails if any loaded Invocation (including a hypothetical fourth list) is missing from all_invocations.
criteria.evidence: All 18 matching tests passed, including store::tests::all_invocations_covers_every_loaded_invocation and the new store::tests::all_roles_lists_every_role_variant. The store test (store.rs:758-802) loads one Invocation per ALL_ROLES entry through from_parts and asserts the (seq, role) pairs from all_invocations equal the input. So a list that from_parts routes to but all_invocations does not chain would fail the test. ALL_ROLES is checked against the Role enum source, so a new role routed to a new list is forced into the test.

criteria.criterion: Dropped, stale and abandoned jobs that never ran a model are excluded from the 8-job window and class totals; a unit test in role_need.rs covers it.
criteria.evidence: The test passed. counts_as_work (role_need.rs:79-89) admits only jobs that closed Landed, Rejected, Failed or TimedOut and have a non-on-demand invocation. The test was already in the base and is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml OLY-9-11 mechanism and measure match the code (all_invocations, on-demand roles not measured, ends with `status: role need`); CHANGELOG.md has an entry naming the root cause; xtask/shard-timings.txt lists any new test binary.
criteria.evidence: spec.toml line 1497 names Records::all_invocations and says the steward, audience and auditor run on demand and are reported as not measured. The measure at line 1499 ends 'status: role need', which matches compute and line(). The new CHANGELOG bullet (line 12) names the root cause: invocations are kept in four places, and nothing guarded the list of sources or roles. It also cites 41539a7 and b670592, and both appear in the evidence history.json. The new tests are unit tests in the athena-core lib, which shard-timings.txt already lists at line 51 ('athena-core --lib'), so no new binary needs a line.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test`; all pass. The new tests fail on the pre-change code (verifier checks by reading the diff for assertions on the auditor/steward/audience outcomes).
criteria.evidence: Athena recorded that fmt, clippy and the tests passed for 98853029 (CI run 43078837334). The diff holds explicit assertions on the steward, audience and auditor outcomes: source == SOURCE_OUTSIDE_JOBS, !flagged, present in not_measured with n > 0, and absent from retire_candidates. Every ALL_ROLES role is also asserted to have count > 0. Athena's run without the fix shows the new tests do not compile on the base, because ALL_ROLES and MEASURED_ROLES are missing. Reading the code shows they would also fail on behavior if compute read job.invocations.

findings.summary: The ALL_ROLES completeness test finds the Role variants by scanning the enum's source text, which is a fragile heuristic.
findings.evidence: The test uses include_str! on athena-data/src/records.rs, splits on 'pub enum Role {' and '\n}', drops lines starting with '///' or '#[', and lowercases each name before calling Role::parse. A `//` comment, a variant with fields, a multi-word variant such as CodeReviewer → 'codereviewer', or a reformat of the enum would make the test fail spuriously or miss a variant. A simpler check that the compiler enforces: a test-only `fn _covers(r: Role) -> usize { match r { Role::Reader => 0, ... } }` with no wildcard arm, indexed into ALL_ROLES. Role::as_str already relies on the same exhaustive match. Any failure is loud, not silent, so this is not a blocker.

findings.summary: The standing test runs on fixtures, not on the real records, so the introspections' suggestion of a real-records replay is only partly taken up.
findings.evidence: All three introspections asked for a measure to be replayed over the real records and checked against roles known to be active. The accepted reading chose a known-active fixture loaded through Records::from_parts, which tests the same routing the real loader uses. `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence>` does not print the role need section, so I could not check the measure on the real records. The working copy has no records/, which is by design.

findings.summary: The 'fails without the fix' evidence for the new tests is a compile failure, not a behavior failure.
findings.evidence: In Athena's fails-without-3, 4 and 5 runs, the tests failed with E0425 because ALL_ROLES and MEASURED_ROLES are missing. The behavior check comes from reading the assertions in the diff, not from a mutation run. The source fix (all_invocations) landed earlier, in 41539a7 and b670592.

summary: The change passes. The source fix (Records::all_invocations, the doc comment on JobRecords::invocations and the system fact) was already in the base. This change adds guards so the same class of failure cannot come back: ALL_ROLES with a check that it lists every Role variant, a store test over every role that every invocation from_parts loads comes back out of all_invocations, MEASURED_ROLES with a check that every role is classified as measured or on demand (exactly one), and an end-to-end RoleNeed::compute test. That test loads every role through from_parts and asserts the steward, audience and auditor are counted from outside job records, reported as not measured, and never retire candidates. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core role_need`, `cargo test -p athena-core store` and the window test, and all passed. The content criteria check out by Grep. CI recorded fmt, clippy and the tests as passing. All changed files are on the deliverables list. Two minor findings: the variant-completeness test scans the enum's source text where an exhaustive match would let the compiler check it, and the standing check runs on fixtures rather than on the real records.
